clue.text: Conservative listing dodgy deal is in the dailies

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the words that follow are not to be trusted in their printed order

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
a ship that is listing is leaning to one side
the fodder letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory politician turns up in the daily papers listing a shady deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dailies' looks like the newspapers, but in British usage a daily is a domestic cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily, in British English, is a woman employed to clean a house each day, so dailies are cleaning ladies.

clue.text: Current record covers showing freshness

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps around it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A recording of electrical current reveals something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is informal for cheeky impudence, and freshness in the sense of sauciness means the same.

clue.text: One single girl from Wales from the east

parts.note: a single one is simply 'a'
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A lone unmarried woman from Wales has come over from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the east' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something Asian originates from the continent of Asia, which lies to the east of Europe.

clue.text: Keen on fixing tungsten objects on the fence

indicators.note: fixing here means securing something in place inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten (wolfram)
to mind something is to object to it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to repair tungsten items finds them stuck on a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' reads as a noun but is the verb: if you mind, you object.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the fence is the idiom for being undecided, which is exactly the state of being in two minds.

clue.text: Manager rolling ciggy before official turns up

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the word for ciggy is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means flipping the word so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official

explanation.surface: A football manager is rolling a cigarette when the referee arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaffer is British slang for a boss, especially a football manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is informal British for the boss or manager, used especially of a football team's manager.

clue.text: See 1
It might help you to see a French city

definitions.text: It might help you to see
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a glass for correcting vision
second meaning: a town in northern France, near Lille

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sightseeing aid; the second half is a proper noun, the French town in the Pas-de-Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is the curved glass in spectacles or a camera that focuses light, and Lens is also a northern French town.

clue.text: Saved extremely delicate wine cups, as it happens

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it in curved hands, so one piece holds another
extremely points to the very ends of the next word, its outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of delicate
red is a type of wine
a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: Someone cradling fine wine glasses, by the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' reads as a throwaway phrase, but it means live, as in a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue or save them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Shows up in empty Epsom watering hole with right idiots

indicators.note: an empty word has had its contents removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of Epsom
a watering hole is informal for a pub or bar
R is the abbreviation for right
asses are fools

explanation.surface: Idiots in a bar at Epsom racecourse turn up and cause a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English town famous for its racecourse, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to make them look foolish, which is what embarrassing them does.

clue.text: It might help with a break in Adriatic resort around November

definitions.text: It might help with a break

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed on both sides of another

parts.note: Split is a Croatian port and resort on the Adriatic
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Croatian seaside town might help someone on a November holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' suggests a holiday, fitting the resort, but it is a broken bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid strip bound to a fractured limb to keep it immobile while the bone heals.

clue.text: Cooler suit for groups of lovers?

parts.note: a fan cools you down
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A more fashionable outfit for couples on a romantic outing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler suit' looks like trendier clothing; it is two separate pieces, a cooling device and a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised group of devoted admirers of a star, so its members are lovers of that celebrity.

clue.text: Given support, papa stops boy hurting daughter

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other like a stopper

parts.note: a son is a boy
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something sore is hurting
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Dad steps in to stop his son hurting his sister, and backs him up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor someone is to back them, typically with money, so sponsored means given support.

clue.text: Awful porkies are told, dismissing old reform agenda

indicators.note: something awful is a terrible mess, so the following letters are jumbled out of order
dismissing means sending away, so the word for elderly is taken out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Terrible lies are being spread, scrapping an old programme of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Porkies is Cockney rhyming slang (pork pies, lies). Remove O-L-D from TOLD, leaving T, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's 1980s programme of restructuring the Soviet economy and political system, a reform agenda.

clue.text: Brief work by bard on American states

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the final letter is lopped off
in an across entry, one thing written on another is placed after it, so the bard's work comes second

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a bard, or poet, writes verse

explanation.surface: A short Shakespeare piece about the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, one piece written on another follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert firmly, so avers means states as a verb.

clue.text: Bathes with Arab, with a desire for a soak?

parts.note: to dip is to bathe briefly
an Omani is an Arab from Oman
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bathes alongside an Arab companion, longing for a long soak in the tub?
explanation.walkthrough: A soak is a heavy drinker, not a bath; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipsomania is a pathological craving for alcohol, and a soak is slang for a drunkard.

clue.text: Rules of game are, we hear, maintained by writer

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: to be maintained by something is to be held up within it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

indicators.note: we hear means take the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: the letter R sounds like the word are

explanation.surface: The rules of a game are said to be kept by the person who wrote them.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is the usual crossword game, and Bic is a ballpoint brand standing in for any pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of instructions or rules, as on an exam paper, originally written in red.

clue.text: Transport group known for flying tours love dry and wet weather

indicators.note: something that tours goes all the way round, so it surrounds the next piece

parts.note: BA is British Airways
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: An airline offers tour packages for those who love dry and rainy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat train is a train timed to connect with a ship at a port, a form of transport.

clue.text: Car — I slip into it

indicators.note: going into something puts one piece inside another

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
taken as written
to err is to make a slip

explanation.surface: Someone tells of sliding into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Sierra was a popular British family car of the 1980s.

clue.text: Quixotic hero has spades, good at practical work

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in cards
a handy person is good at practical jobs

explanation.surface: Don Quixote's sidekick is good with a spade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quixotic hero' suggests Don Quixote or Sancho Panza, but it is Tristram Shandy, hero of Sterne's novel, which owes much to Cervantes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is the eccentric, whimsical hero of Laurence Sterne's comic novel, a work full of quixotic digressions.

clue.text: Also leaving Spain, making tracks

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for the country goes away

parts.note: besides means also
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Someone is also departing Spain, heading off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making tracks' is an idiom for leaving; here tracks are recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: B-sides are the secondary tracks on the reverse of a single record.

clue.text: Prow of sailing boat in outline

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a vessel, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of sailing
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The bow of a yacht seen in silhouette.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or summary, giving the outline of something.

clue.text: Jalopy's constant speed

parts.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: An old banger keeps going at a steady speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for an old, ramshackle vehicle, just as a jalopy is a battered old car.

clue.text: KGB, say, saving Philby time, which is most revealing

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: the Soviet KGB employed spies
Kim Philby was a British double agent for the Soviets
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The KGB rescuing the defector Philby: how much that exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Philby's first name is the piece needed; he was the most famous of the Cambridge spies who worked for Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpiest describes the scantiest clothing, which therefore shows off, or reveals, the most of the body.

clue.text: Force has trouble-maker held after dropping case

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer shell, so dropping it removes the first and last letters

parts.note: an imp is a mischief-maker
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police detain a troublemaker after a dropped court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or compel them to act, so it means to force.

clue.text: Speculator saving banks close to collapse

indicators.note: banks surround a river on both sides, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: saving means except, as does bar

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of collapse

explanation.surface: A City trader hoards money as the banks near collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like financial institutions; it is the verb to bank, enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear is a stock-market speculator who sells expecting prices to fall.

clue.text: Fun activity dressing nurses in tissue

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something cradled, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds
a game is a fun activity

explanation.surface: A playful bandaging session as nurses practise on tissues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like hospital staff, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of tough fibrous connective tissue linking bones at a joint.

clue.text: Head salesman to criticise returns

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: The chief salesman finds critics returning his products.
explanation.definitionFit: Napper is old British slang for the head.

clue.text: Age of American figure finally raised

definitions.note: EON is the American spelling of aeon

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the final letter lifts it from the bottom to the top

parts.note: one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: How old a statue of a famous American is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of American' marks the US spelling: British English writes aeon.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period, an age, and eon without the A is the US spelling.

clue.text: Big news! Princess in Britain was forced to ingest ecstasy and cocaine?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for Britain
Princess Anne is the British monarch's sister

indicators.note: to ingest is to swallow, so a piece is taken inside another

parts.note: had (to) means was forced to
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a line is a dose of cocaine laid out for snorting

explanation.surface: A tabloid splash: a British princess was made to take drugs?
explanation.definitionFit: A banner headline runs across the full width of a front page, used for the biggest news stories.

clue.text: See 28
